claims.text: PbTe is a semiconductor or thermoelectric material suitable for testing the proposed lattice-thermal-conductivity effect.
Introducing SRO precipitates into PbTe or a similar material will reduce phonon scattering times.
Introducing SRO precipitates will lower lattice thermal conductivity relative to pristine material.
Pristine PbTe has relatively long phonon mean free paths.
Pristine PbTe has relatively high lattice thermal conductivity compared with the proposed SRO-containing state.
Controlled doping or thermal treatment can promote the formation of SRO precipitates.
Processing temperature and dopant concentration can be selected to favor SRO precipitates while largely preserving electronic conduction.
There is a measurement temperature range in which phonon scattering dominates the relevant heat-transport behavior.
SRO precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers in the crystal lattice.
Disruption of lattice periodicity by SRO precipitates enhances phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces the average phonon mean free path.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces the phonon scattering time.
Reduced phonon mean free path and scattering time lower the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity.
The magnitude of the lattice-thermal-conductivity reduction will correlate with SRO precipitate density and spatial distribution.
The proposed effect depends on optimizing precipitate density.
Excessive precipitation may introduce defects or other scattering effects that impair charge-carrier transport and complicate thermal and electrical transport.
The conductivity reduction may depend on precipitate nature and distribution, electron-phonon coupling, and carrier concentration.
